source.title: Corpus transnuméré du linéaire A (deuxième édition)
source.series: Bibliothèque des Cahiers de Linguistique de Louvain (BCLL) 74

observed_methodological_description: The editors reviewed/re-examined Linear A texts rather than merely publishing an index.
The review reports comparison of their readings with good photographs and new facsimiles where available.
The review describes new or corrected readings and an apparatus/commentary layer.
editorial_independence_evidence_before_a.why_promising: This is compatible with an alternate editorial re-reading lineage and is therefore a strong R3B acquisition candidate.
editorial_independence_evidence_before_a.why_not_yet_L2_or_L3: A review and bibliographic description do not establish the exact provenance of every transcription token, the degree of dependence on GORILA/earlier corpora, or the independence class of the acquired edition bytes.

preferred_request_order.request: Ask Peeters whether a lawful digital research copy/electronic archive of CTLA second edition exists and can be supplied or accessed under research-use/copyright restrictions.
Ask whether legacy production/typesetting files or an author/publisher-approved digital transcription source survive and can be made available for non-redistributive reproducibility research.

If only physical copies are available, ask whether Peeters can identify an institutional digital archive, rights holder, author estate/archive, or library holding an authorized digital preservation copy suitable for research access.

provenance_questions_before_R3B_credit: For the second edition, which inscriptions/readings were rechecked directly against photographs, facsimiles, autography or primary excavation publications?
Which portions, if any, were transcribed or normalized from GORILA or another existing transcription corpus without independent re-reading?
Does the edition preserve source-native uncertainty, damage, line/surface boundaries, numerics and sign alternatives in a mechanically recoverable form?
Are the corrected/new readings traceable to an editorial apparatus or explicit source references?
Can a stable document-identity bridge to GORILA/mwenge be constructed without consulting transcription content?
upon_receipt: Run generic source-intake quarantine before semantic inspection.
Preserve original publisher/library bytes and compute SHA-256/byte length.
Apply frozen R3B-0 acquisition receipt contract and record copyright/access basis.
Classify transcription/editorial provenance before assigning L1/L2/L3.
If provenance permits, build scientific-content-excluded identity inventory and execute frozen R3B-1 overlap partition before candidate inspection.

suggested_email.subject: Research access inquiry: Corpus transnuméré du linéaire A, 2nd ed. (BCLL 74, 1994)
suggested_email.body:
Dear Peeters Publishers,

I am conducting a non-commercial reproducibility study comparing scholarly Linear A transcription editions and am trying to locate a lawful digital research copy or archival electronic source for J. Raison & M. Pope, Corpus transnuméré du linéaire A (deuxième édition), BCLL 74, 1994, ISBN 978-90-6831-561-5.

Your current catalogue still lists the volume. Could you please let me know whether a digital research copy, electronic archival copy, or legacy production/typesetting files exist and whether research access can be granted under appropriate copyright/use restrictions? I do not intend to redistribute the work.

The study requires preserving the edition exactly as received and comparing transcription provenance and editorial differences before testing individual readings. If Peeters does not hold a digital copy, I would also be grateful for any information on an institutional archive, rights holder, author archive/estate, or library that may hold an authorized digital preservation copy.

The purpose is cross-edition transcription reproducibility, not a decipherment claim. Any access, citation, storage or non-redistribution conditions would be respected.

Thank you very much for your help.

Best regards,
Oleksandr Ahapov / Hawkar
